subject: Anxiety does not knock first
preview: What Jesus said about worry, for the busiest weeks of the year.
linkText: What Does the Bible Say About Anxiety? A Complete Guide for Christians

blocks.text: Anxiety does not knock first.
It shows up in the middle of the night.
It shows up when the bank account is low and the Christmas list is not.
It follows you into the family dinner and sits in your chest the whole time.
And sometimes another Christian tells you to just have more faith.
That one stings the most.
Because it makes your anxiety feel like proof that something is wrong with your walk with God.
Here is what I want you to hear. You are not a bad Christian.
David lay awake at night, soaking his bed with tears.
Martha was so anxious about serving dinner that she missed Jesus sitting in her living room.
Jesus did not scold her for the dinner. He named what was happening inside her.
"Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things."
God does not give anxiety a rebuke. He gives it a replacement.
"Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."
In the old King James language, "be careful for nothing" means be anxious about nothing.
Then comes the promise. The peace of God "shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."
That word keep means to guard, like a soldier standing watch at the gate.
Faith is not the absence of anxiety. Faith is where you carry it.
So this week, when the spiral starts, say the worry to God out loud, by name.
And if anxiety is crushing you day after day, seeing a doctor or counselor is not weak faith. God works through wise helpers too.
In the full guide I walk through what Jesus taught about worry, five verses to hold onto, and honest answers to questions like whether anxiety is a sin.
